subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw make gateway ownership of the live shared state DB enforceable by RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI access, by a stricter single-writer lease, or by combining both?
rationale: The source-visible issue is not just a narrow bug in one command; it defines which process may configure, migrate, write, or checkpoint the shared state DB while the gateway is running.

options.title: RPC-first plus active lease guard
options.body: Prefer Gateway RPC for health/status/stability and refuse CLI write/checkpoint/migration opens while the gateway owns the live DB, leaving explicit offline doctor repair as the migration path.

options.title: No-maintenance CLI reads only
options.body: Keep CLI diagnostics file-backed where needed, but add a read-only open mode that skips WAL setup, checkpoints, schema migrations, and plugin-state probe writes under an active gateway.

options.title: Gateway-only SQLite ownership
options.body: Make the gateway the sole process that ever opens the shared DB read-write during normal operation, pushing all live diagnostics through RPC and reserving file access for stopped-gateway recovery.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus active lease guard
recommendation.body: Prefer Gateway RPC for health/status/stability and refuse CLI write/checkpoint/migration opens while the gateway owns the live DB, leaving explicit offline doctor repair as the migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice crosses core runtime state ownership and CLI/gateway product policy, and steipete authored the runtime SQLite refactor that established this boundary.
